title: Forecasting: Principles and Practice, third edition — Time series cross-validation
authors_or_org: Rob J Hyndman and George Athanasopoulos
published_or_version: Third edition, online chapter accessed 2026-10-24; historical /tscv.html redirects to /toolbox.html
supported_claim: Rolling forecast origins train on preceding data and can score multistep horizons; residual fit is not out-of-sample forecast accuracy.
limitations: General forecasting methodology; does not establish sufficient enterprise sample size, optimal AI-spend horizon, or a particular model winner.
license_status: Reuse license not verified in this review; citation and original paraphrase only.

title: Evaluating time series forecasting models: An empirical study on performance estimation methods
authors_or_org: Vitor Cerqueira, Luis Torgo, Igor Mozetič
published_or_version: Machine Learning, January 2020 according to author publication page
kind: Primary empirical research, author publication page
supported_claim: Comparison across 174 real series and three synthetic series found performance-estimation results depend on stationarity; repeated out-of-sample methods performed better in nonstationary cases in that study.
limitations: Study-specific empirical findings; author abstract inspected, not full experimental replication; no universal theorem that chronological holdout dominates all cross-validation.
license_status: Page and article reuse licenses not verified.

title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
authors_or_org: Gavin C. Cawley and Nicola L. C. Talbot
supported_claim: Optimizing a finite-sample selection criterion can overfit that criterion and bias reported generalization performance; evaluating the selected procedure requires separation from its tuning data.
limitations: Not an AI-spend study; does not prescribe the exact chronological/calibration split or compute budget proposed here.
license_status: PDF identifies copyright 2010 Cawley and Talbot; reuse license not independently verified.

title: Generalization in Adaptive Data Analysis and Holdout Reuse
authors_or_org: Cynthia Dwork, Vitaly Feldman, Moritz Hardt, Toniann Pitassi, Omer Reingold and Aaron Roth
supported_claim: Adaptively reusing ordinary holdout feedback can overfit it; specialized mechanisms provide validity guarantees under specified assumptions.
limitations: The track does not implement a reusable-holdout mechanism or claim its guarantees transfer automatically to dependent enterprise time series.
license_status: arXiv reuse-license link exists; exact license not verified.

title: ALFRED Download Data Help
authors_or_org: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
supported_claim: Observation dates, initial releases, revision vintages and real-time validity periods represent different information; historical vintages recover data as available then.
limitations: Macroeconomic data precedent only; source does not establish billing completion or a universal settlement lag.
license_status: Documentation reuse terms not verified; constituent economic-series rights are not inferred from the host.

title: Strictly Proper Scoring Rules, Prediction, and Estimation
authors_or_org: Tilmann Gneiting and Adrian E. Raftery
published_or_version: Journal of the American Statistical Association 102(477), March 2007; DOI 10.1198/016214506000001437
supported_claim: Proper scoring rules encourage honest distributional reporting; CRPS, quantile and interval scores support probabilistic evaluation beyond point accuracy or coverage alone.
limitations: Score propriety does not establish empirical calibration, finite-sample support, business utility, or joint dependence quality from marginal scores.
license_status: PDF states copyright 2007 American Statistical Association; no broad reuse permission verified.

title: Evaluating epidemic forecasts in an interval format, with 2022 correction
authors_or_org: Johannes Bracher, Evan L. Ray, Tilmann Gneiting and Nicholas G. Reich
published_or_version: 12 February 2021, PLOS Computational Biology 17(2):e1008618; correction 5 October 2022, e1010592
supported_claim: WIS scores quantile/interval forecasts with width and over/underprediction components; full-density log scoring cannot be computed merely from interval outputs. Correction fixes example score values and figures, not the general recommendation.
limitations: Epidemic application does not validate enterprise spending. Implementers must inspect correction at https://journals.plos.org/ploscompbiol/article?id=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1010592 and use a shared quantile grid.
license_status: Article and correction explicitly state Creative Commons Attribution License; linked legal version not separately inspected. Linked code/dataset licenses not verified.

title: Comparing Predictive Accuracy
authors_or_org: Francis X. Diebold and Roberto S. Mariano
published_or_version: Journal of Business & Economic Statistics 13(3):253–263, 1995; publisher page lists online publication 2 July 2012
supported_claim: Forecast-comparison testing can handle varied losses and serially/contemporaneously correlated forecast errors under its stated inferential conditions.
limitations: Publisher search result exposed primary abstract; direct page open returned 403. No claim that one off-the-shelf test controls arbitrary multi-tenant, multi-horizon, adaptive comparisons; small dependent samples remain a concern.

title: Effective forecasting and judgmental adjustments: an empirical evaluation and strategies for improvement in supply-chain planning
authors_or_org: Robert Fildes, Paul Goodwin, Michael Lawrence and Konstantinos Nikolopoulos
kind: Primary empirical research, institutional author repository
supported_claim: In a study of over 60,000 forecasts from four supply-chain companies, judgmental adjustments improved average accuracy in three companies but small and upward adjustments often harmed accuracy.
limitations: Repository exposes abstract and explicitly says full text unavailable there. Domain-specific evidence cannot establish the sign of manager bias for AI spending, and budgets may not be predictive forecasts.
license_status: Article reuse license not verified; institutional page is not evidence that underlying data are reusable.

title: AI Agents That Matter
authors_or_org: Sayash Kapoor, Benedikt Stroebl, Zachary S. Siegel, Nitya Nadgir and Arvind Narayanan
published_or_version: arXiv:2407.01502v1, 1 July 2024; a later TMLR version surfaced but is not the cited inspected version
supported_claim: Agent comparisons should account for cost, reproducibility and suitable holdouts; benchmark optimization can fail to establish downstream usefulness.
limitations: Not a forecasting-selector experiment; exact budget-matched search and prospective policies in this track are proposed adaptations.
license_status: arXiv reuse-license details not verified; code or benchmark rights not inferred.

title: GIFT-Eval: A Benchmark For General Time Series Forecasting Model Evaluation
authors_or_org: Taha Aksu, Gerald Woo, Juncheng Liu, Xu Liu, Chenghao Liu, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong and Doyen Sahoo
supported_claim: General forecasting benchmarks span heterogeneous datasets/horizons and make pretraining/test leakage an explicit concern; such breadth is useful engineering evidence.
limitations: No representative enterprise AI-spend, billing-revision, staffing, manager or internal-budget population established. A claimed non-leaking benchmark does not certify every later model's training corpus.
